questions.q: Metrics, logs, and traces each answer a different question. What are metrics best for?
options: Recording the full payload of each failed request for debugging
Following one request's path across many collaborating services
Cheap aggregate time-series like rates, latencies, and saturation over time
Storing structured audit events for compliance review

questions.q: Why do latency SLOs use percentiles like p99 instead of the mean?
options: Means hide tail pain; a fine average can coexist with terrible worst-case latency
Percentiles are cheaper to compute than a running average
Computing a true mean requires storing every raw sample, which is infeasible at scale
p99 automatically excludes bot and health-check traffic

questions.q: What is an SLI, concretely?
options: A contract promising customers refunds if uptime drops
The internal numerical target your team formally commits to for a given metric
A dashboard panel that pages on-call when it turns red
A measured signal of service health, like fraction of successful requests

questions.q: What is the purpose of an error budget?
options: Money reserved each quarter specifically for incident response tooling and training
An allowed amount of unreliability to spend on risk and change
The maximum number of known bugs a release may ship with
Headcount allocated to fixing production errors each sprint

questions.q: What distinguishes structured logging from plain text logs?
options: Machine-parseable key-value fields enabling reliable filtering and aggregation
Structured logs are encrypted at rest while text logs are not
Structured logs bypass local disk entirely, streaming straight to the collector service
A fixed 80-character line format optimized for terminals

questions.q: In distributed tracing, what is a span?
options: The complete end-to-end journey of one request across every participating service
The network hop between two adjacent services
A single timed operation within a trace, with parent-child links
The sampling window during which traces are recorded

questions.q: How does a trace stay connected as a request crosses service boundaries?
options: Each service logs to a shared file that the tracer tails
Trace and span IDs propagate in request headers or message metadata
The load balancer records every hop centrally
Precisely clock-synchronized timestamps let the backend infer the request path afterward

questions.q: Which alerting philosophy reduces pager fatigue?
options: Page the on-call for every detected anomaly so that nothing is ever missed
Route all alerts to email so they can be batched
Page only during business hours, deferring the rest
Page on user-impacting symptoms; ticket the merely suspicious causes

questions.q: p50 is 40 ms, p99 is 2 s. What does this shape usually indicate?
options: Monitoring overhead itself adds two full seconds to one request out of every hundred
The service is uniformly slow and needs a faster runtime
The p99 metric is misconfigured, since it cannot exceed 10x p50
Most requests are fine, but a tail (GC, cold caches, slow deps) is badly degraded

questions.q: Why do high-traffic systems sample traces instead of recording all of them?
options: Full tracing's storage and overhead cost outweighs its debugging value at scale
Most tracing libraries hard-cap their throughput at a few hundred spans per second
Unsampled traces violate data-retention regulations
Sampling improves trace accuracy by removing noisy requests

questions.q: An SLO is 99.9% success over 30 days. Roughly how much full downtime does that budget allow?
options: About 4.3 hours
About 43 minutes
About 4.3 minutes
About 7.2 hours

questions.q: Error rate spiked, but only logs exist, no metrics. What is the practical pain?
options: Logging frameworks cannot record genuine errors at all, only warnings and info lines
Log storage costs make retention beyond a day impossible
Quantifying rate and trends means expensive ad-hoc log scans instead of a cheap query
Errors in logs are unordered, making causality unknowable

questions.q: A trace shows 800 ms total: gateway 20 ms, service A 30 ms, then a 700 ms gap before service B's span. Likely culprit?
options: Service B's business logic, which the span understates
Queueing or connection wait between A and B not captured by either span
The API gateway itself, because it is the component that initiated the request
Clock skew, which always manifests as gaps this large

questions.q: Your team burns 80% of the monthly error budget in week one. What does SRE practice suggest?
options: Redefine the SLO upward so the budget resets immediately
Silence the noisiest alerts for the remainder of the month to reduce pager noise
Spend the remaining budget on a planned chaos experiment
Slow risky launches and prioritize reliability work until the budget recovers

questions.q: Logs from 40 services use inconsistent request ID field names. What is the highest-leverage fix?
options: Grep with 40 alternate patterns and save it as a runbook
Rely on timestamps to join related logs across the services
Standardize a correlation ID field and propagate it in every service's logs
Centralize all the log files onto a single host so that field names stop mattering

questions.q: Why alert on burn rate (budget consumption speed) rather than raw error thresholds?
options: It ties alert urgency to real SLO impact, catching both fast and slow burns
Burn rate is cheaper to compute than an error ratio
Raw error-rate ratios cannot be measured reliably by modern metric collection agents
Burn rate alerts never fire during deployments

questions.q: After adding 100% tracing to a hot service, p99 latency rises 15%. Most plausible mechanism?
options: Span creation and export contend for CPU and network on the request path
Traces are stored in the same database as user data, causing lock contention
The trace collector rejects spans, forcing synchronous retries by default
Sampling at 100% disables the JIT compiler in most runtimes

questions.q: An outage went unnoticed: dashboards were green because the metrics pipeline itself had failed. What prevents this blind spot?
options: Rendering dashboards from raw logs instead of metrics
Meta-monitoring with heartbeats, plus alerting on absent data, from independent infrastructure
Doubling scrape frequency so gaps close twice as fast
Snapshotting dashboards hourly for later comparison

questions.q: You must keep 13 months of metrics for capacity planning without huge storage bills. Standard approach?
options: Persist only p50 values, since medians define capacity
Retain raw resolution for every series and just buy cheaper disks each year
Store metrics as compressed log lines and re-parse when needed
Downsample: raw short-term, progressively coarser rollups for older data

questions.q: One user reports sporadic 500s; overall error rate is 0.01% and alerts are silent. Which capability finds the cause fastest?
options: A CPU profiler attached to every production instance
Raising alert sensitivity until the sporadic errors trigger a page
Exemplar traces linked from error metrics, filterable by user or request attributes
A synthetic probe replaying the user's typical journey hourly
